## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: departures from Burnham's top-18 cabinet between 1 Sep and 31 Dec 2026 (compiled 30 Sep 2026)

## 1. Resolution sources

- **Both cited sources were blocked (HTTP 403 on 2026-09-30):**
  - members.parliament.uk/government/cabinet
  - metaculus.com/questions/45250, and its API endpoint
  - So I cannot report the parliament page wording, the Metaculus text, the community forecast or any comments.
- **GOV.UK ministers page (https://www.gov.uk/government/ministers, fetched 2026-09-30):**
  - Andy Burnham is PM.
  - All 18 people in the fine print hold the posts listed there. There are no personnel differences.
  - Only the formatting differs: "Dame Angela Eagle", "Sir Chris Bryant", and Business also carries "President of the Board of Trade".
  - GOV.UK may lag behind real changes.
- **Other cabinet members, outside the 18:** Anneliese Midgley (Chief Whip), Baroness Smith of Basildon (Lords Leader), Sir Alan Campbell (Commons Leader), Bridget Phillipson (Women and Equalities) and Emma Reynolds (Chief Secretary to the Treasury).
  - Lords members could never count anyway, since the question covers MPs only.
- **Departures so far:** Wikipedia's Burnham ministry page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnham_ministry) and news searches show **no departures from the 18 between 20 Jul and 30 Sep 2026**. Confidence is moderate.
- **Status: the count stands at 0 as of 30 Sep 2026**, with 3 months left (1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026).
- **Timing:** the Metaculus question opened on 2026-09-28. Anything before 1 Sep does not count.

## 2. Context and recent news

**How Burnham became PM** (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Labour_Party_leadership_crisis)
- 7 May 2026: Labour did badly in the local elections.
- 12 May: Fahnbulleh resigned calling for Starmer to go.
- 14 May: Streeting resigned as Health Secretary.
- 11 Jun: Healey resigned over defence spending.
- 18 Jun: Burnham won the Makerfield by-election.
- 22 Jun: Starmer announced his resignation (TIME, https://time.com/article/2026/06/22/uk-prime-minister-keir-starmer-resignation-reports-burnham-leadership-potential/).
- 17 Jul: Burnham was elected Labour leader unopposed.
- 20 Jul: Burnham became PM.

**Cabinet formation (20–23 Jul 2026)**
- 15 cabinet members were dismissed. Sources: https://www.politics.co.uk/news/2026/07/20/andy-burnham-appoints-new-cabinet-whos-in-and-whos-out/ and https://www.itv.com/news/2026-07-21/andy-burnhams-cabinet-whos-in-and-whos-out
- Several of those sacked are now on the backbenches. Peter Kyle has been publicly critical (HuffPost, 26 Sep).

**1 Sep 2026: Starmer quit as an MP**
- This triggered the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, set for **8 Oct 2026**.
- There are 15 candidates, including Green leader Zack Polanski (https://labourlist.org/2026/09/holborn-st-pancras-by-election-date/).

**14 Sep: devolved leaders' pact**
- The Scottish, Welsh and Northern Ireland leaders signed a self-determination pact (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/14/leaders-of-scotland-wales-northern-ireland-unite-for-self-determination).
- Burnham has ruled out giving Wales powers for an independence referendum.

**22 Sep: "Ministry of Truth" row**
- Burnham announced a National Centre for Information Defence, and critics attacked it as a threat to free speech (https://ground.news/article/andy-burnhams-ministry-of-truth).

**~25–27 Sep: open cabinet split, Rayner vs Mahmood — the main live flashpoint**
- The dispute is over Mahmood's plan to raise the settlement wait for care workers from 5 to 15 years.
- Rayner called it "very disruptive" in The Times. Reports also quote her calling it "un-British".
- Over 100 Labour MPs and the unions oppose the plan. Nandy backed Mahmood.
- Rayner denied there is a split. Mahmood has hinted she may water the plan down.
- Sources:
  - HuffPost, 26 Sep: https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/cabinet-split-angela-rayner-shabana-mahmood_uk_6ab77bbde4b07795582c58c5
  - LBC: https://www.lbc.co.uk/article/angela-rayner-attacks-migrant-visa-changes-5Hjdj6k_2/

**Labour conference, Liverpool (~27–30 Sep)**
- 28 Sep: Healey's speech committed to the fiscal rules. He has reportedly lost about half of his £23.6bn headroom (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-28/healey-says-hope-for-britons-is-earned-through-fiscal-discipline).
- 29 Sep: Burnham gave his conference speech.

**29 Sep: political climate (CNN, via https://kesq.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2026/09/29/britains-pm-is-on-a-burnham-bounce-when-will-he-fall-to-earth/)**
- Labour narrowly leads Reform in the polls.
- The Iran war and Middle East situation are pushing up energy prices and inflation.
- Burnham has ruled out an early election; the next is due by Aug 2029.

**Rayner's tax affairs**
- HMRC cleared her around 14 May 2026 (https://www.itv.com/news/2026-05-14/angela-rayner-says-she-has-been-cleared-by-hmrc-after-stamp-duty-row).
- I found no new tax story since then.

**Nothing found on the rest**
- No standards investigations or reshuffle rumours surfaced for any of the 18.
- There was no specific news since July on Norris, Powell, McFadden, J. Reynolds, H. Alexander, Fahnbulleh, Eagle, Bryant, D. Alexander, Kinnock, Cooper, Miliband or Haigh.

**Scheduled before 1 Jan 2027**
- 8 Oct: Holborn and St Pancras by-election.
- 28 Oct: Healey's first Budget, expected to be difficult (https://www.professionalpensions.com/news/4533779/government-confirms-date-autumn-budget-2026).
- Pending: Mahmood's decision on the care-worker visa plan.
- No reshuffle is scheduled and no early election is expected.

**Prediction markets (Polymarket, seen 30 Sep 2026)**
- "Who will be the first to leave the Burnham Cabinet?": Healey leads at 14%, with the other names' prices not seen. Volume is ~$124K and liquidity ~$221K.
  - This market has no deadline tied to 2026, so it does not map directly onto this question.
- "UK election called by 30 Jun 2027": 23% yes, volume ~$831K.
- "How many UK PMs by end of 2027?": "2" at 88%, volume ~$153K.
- I found no Kalshi market on cabinet departures.

## 3. Base rates

Dates marked [mem] come from the subagent's memory and were not checked against a source.

**Departures from top cabinet posts in a new PM's first ~6 months**
- At least one departure in 5 of 8 cases: Truss, Sunak, Johnson, Cameron and Starmer.
  - Starmer: Haigh resigned Nov 2024, in month 5 [mem].
  - Sunak: Williamson went in week 2 and Zahawi was sacked in month 3.
  - Truss: Kwarteng was sacked and Braverman resigned within 6 weeks [mem].
  - Johnson: Rudd resigned in week 7 [mem].
  - Cameron: Laws resigned 17 days in [mem].
- None in 3 cases: May 2016, Brown 2007 and Blair 1997 [mem].
- The positive cases cluster in the unstable 2019–24 period.

**Any Sep–Dec window**
- Examples with at least one top-level departure: 2017 (3 departures — Fallon, Patel, Green), 2019, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. These are hand-picked examples, not a systematic count.
- Three or more departures in one 4-month window without a reshuffle is rare. 2017 is the clearest case.
- The subagent's rough estimate is about 1–2 unforced departures per cabinet per year, i.e. about 0.3–0.6 per 4-month window. This is its own heuristic, not a figure from a source.

**Planned reshuffles**
- Full reshuffles rarely come in the first 6 months.
- First reshuffles came in month 7 for Johnson (Feb 2020), and month 14 for both Starmer (Sep 2025) and Blair (Jul 1998).
- Early exits are mostly driven by scandal or conduct, not planned.

**Tenure**
- IfG: the average cabinet minister's tenure since 1997 is under 2 years (https://www.instituteforgovernment.org.uk/explainer/government-reshuffles, updated 13 Aug 2026).

**Other sources used**
- https://www.instituteforgovernment.org.uk/comment/seven-things-learned-keir-starmers-first-reshuffle
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_departures_from_the_second_May_ministry (used via a search summary only)

## Caveats

- I could not see the exact resolution-source text or the Metaculus page because both returned 403.
- News coverage runs only to about 29 Sep 2026.
- Several historical dates are from memory and unchecked [mem].

criterios:
This question will resolve as the total number of Members of Parliament acting as one of the top 18 ranked cabinet members (as of July 20, 2026) who leave their positions after September 1, 2026 and before January 1, 2027. Any reason for leaving cabinet positions will count. If three or more cabinet members leave their positions, this question will resolve to **3 or more**.

If the Prime Minister changes during this period the question will resolve to the number as of that date.

[His Majesty's Government: The Cabinet](https://members.parliament.uk/government/cabinet) webpage will be used for resolution.

(a) **Time left:** about 3 months. The window runs 1 Sep to 31 Dec 2026, and September appears to have passed with no departures. The answer will be known on 1 Jan 2027.

(b) **Status quo:** 0. All 18 listed incumbents still hold their posts as of 30 Sep, per GOV.UK and the lack of any departure news.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Unforced top-cabinet departures run at roughly 1–2 per cabinet per year. That implies about 0.3–0.5 expected departures from these 18 posts over the remaining three months.
- New PMs rarely hold a planned reshuffle within six months. Burnham will only be 5 months in by year-end.
- Early departures under new PMs do happen fairly often, but they are mostly scandal-driven and clustered in the unstable 2019–24 period.
- Three or more departures in a single Sep–Dec window without a reshuffle is rare (2017 is the clearest case).
- A Poisson model with an expected value of about 0.45 gives roughly 64% for 0, 29% for 1, 6% for 2 and 1% for 3 or more. I widen the tails to reflect current instability.

Live risks that could add departures:
- the open split between Rayner and Mahmood over the care-worker visa plan;
- Healey's difficult first Budget on 28 Oct, with reduced fiscal headroom;
- a possible loss of the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on 8 Oct to the Greens;
- energy-price inflation driven by the Middle East situation.

The Polymarket price of 14% for Healey leaving first has no deadline, so it only weakly signals that he is the most at risk.

(d) **Unexpected scenario:** Labour loses the by-election and the Budget goes down badly, triggering a backbench revolt. Rayner resigns over the immigration row, Healey is moved after the Budget fallout, and Burnham responds with a mini-reshuffle before Christmas that moves several of the 18 cabinet ministers. That would produce 3 or more departures.
